yasmin (People Ops): Quick sync — Mohammed joined as UK contractor in Jan, converted to UK employee 2026-04-01, but payroll feed shows US federal withholding on Apr payrun (he's UK tax resident). Looks like payroll code defaulted to US tax profile. Need urgent correction + potential W-2c if we already reported. @josh can you confirm what was applied?

josh (Payroll): Confirmed Apr net pay had 10% US federal withholding (federal tax code). System fell back to the US profile because employee record had legacy US address on file. We flagged the Apr payrun after run. If year-to-date US withholding >0, we'll need to prepare a reversal and coordinate with tax to avoid double reporting.

claire (Finance Ops): Cash-wise we can do an off-cycle gross-up or net reversal. If US withholdings were remitted to IRS already, reclaim route is messy. Do we know if deposits were made? @josh any ACH remits?

josh (Payroll): ACH remits for the Apr payrun hit the US tax vendor on 2026-04-07. So taxes likely deposited. We should: (1) correct internal payroll ledger with JE; (2) prepare W-2c if IRS reporting requires; (3) file UK PAYE correction. Need Tax team input on cross-border reporting.

mohammed (Employee): I'm UK resident and have UK NI/UTR. I updated my home address in People Ops on 2026-03-28 — not sure why US profile lingered. Happy to provide any docs. I'm worried about tax filings.

amy (Tax): On it. If US remittance occurred we have two options: reclaim from IRS (rare) or process employee gross-up and report W-2c to correct federal tax amounts. For UK side we'll submit PAYE correction to HMRC to remove duplicate withholding. We'll need: proof of UK residency, UTR, payroll file showing misapplied US withholding, and copies of remittance receipts. Also confirm whether Mohammed received any IRS Form 1042-S (unlikely) — he should not.

claire (Finance Ops): I'll pull the remittance receipts and bank confirmations. Creating JE template now. Suggest JE code: "JE-2026-132-foreign-tax-mispost". Will upload to finance drive.

josh (Payroll): I'll rollback the Apr tax lines in payroll system and create a reversal pay event. Tagging the payrun `mis-tax-profile`. Off-cycle to net correct could be processed but prefer to do net reversal + W-2c to keep records tidy.

yasmin (People Ops): Approved — proceed with payroll reversal and tax-team workflow. Mohammed, please send UTR & proof of UK tax residency to people-ops@redwood.com. Also ping your manager for sign-off for any off-cycle if needed.

mohammed (Employee): Uploaded UTR and UK payslips to my HR folder (onboard/mohammed/uk-tax). Manager approved making-me-whole action. Thanks team.

amy (Tax): Received docs. We'll draft W-2c guidance and coordinate with external counsel on the IRS reclaim feasibility. If reclaim is impossible, W-2c + net reimbursement is the path. Also preparing HMRC adjustment instructions.

payroll-bot: Action logged: TAX-INCIDENT-2398765432. Payroll reversal queued (job 27789). Requires JE and tax docs before finalize. https://payroll.redwood.com/jobs/27789 :clipboard:

josh (Payroll): I've attached the Apr remittance PDF and queued the reversal job. Will wait for JE id before executing.

claire (Finance Ops): JE created: JE-2026-132 ("Foreign tax misposting reversal - Mohammed"). Uploaded to finance drive and linked to TAX-INCIDENT-2398765432.

josh (Payroll): Running reversal now. Will also mark for year-end W-2c if IRS confirms deposit cannot be reclaimed. Will update when reversal completes.

mohammed (Employee): Thank you all 60a appreciate the quick response. Please confirm when reversal posts so I can reconcile my bank statements.

josh (Payroll): Reversal processed 4c4 job 27789 completed. Net adjustment credited to Mohammed's Apr off-cycle run; tax team will advise on W-2c next steps. Closing here once tax confirms.

amy (Tax): We'll decide on W-2c within 5-7 business days after checking remittance trace. If W-2c needed, Tax will draft and People Ops will notify Mohammed.

yasmin (People Ops): Thanks team 44d closing for now, will reopen if Tax needs more info.
